ticket.title: plan blueprints can be orphaned or point at files that do not exist, and no command notices
ticket.description: Measured 2026-11-10 while reminting every member store (GB-347). Plan blueprints and the tickets that name them are not checked against each other, so a store can hold a plan nobody owns and a ticket can point at a file that does not exist - and no command says so.  chalkline: plans/GB-18.md has no owning ticket (no GB-18 in that store); CH-1 and CH-2 report plan_file_path .gaugeblock/storypole/plans/CH-1.md and CH-2.md, and neither file exists. The pointers were dangling before the remint as GB-91.md and GB-102.md and are still dangling after it.  benchwork: plans/GB-17.md and plans/GB-46.md have no owning ticket.  storypole: plans/GB-36.md has no owning ticket.  remint cannot fix this by design - it renames a blueprint when a ticket owns the key, and there is nothing to rename an orphan after - so the orphans survive a migration that is otherwise exhaustive. The check that would catch it is cheap: for every store, name each plan file with no owning ticket and each plan_file_path that resolves to nothing. `ledger-verify` is the natural home, alongside the structural ledger checks it already performs.
